source_snapshot.procedure: On BMC UART confirm standby, run `/usr/bin/powerctrl.sh power_on`, then verify power ON and normal operation.
source_snapshot.criteria: Command succeeds and system powers on; collect evidence/photos/logs.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL; incorrectly proposes host SSH while host is in standby.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: RPUC/high; adds standby/recovery gates but retains infeasible host-SSH transport.

old_problem: Always-on script domain, GPIO target/pulse/idempotence semantics, authoritative standby oracle, rail/POST/OS timing, secure controller transport, one-transition recovery and complete boot-health criteria are undefined.
disposition_reason: A host in standby cannot originate the proposed OS SSH command. ED-18 requires the complete state transition through OS Ready and ED-06 distinguishes it from reboot/cycle variants; ED-03 prevents guessing the always-on controller or GPIO semantics.
decision_basis: Read XLSX row148, same-row AI fields and history2535; exact V002 identity preserved.
Preserved BMC-UART context, standby precondition, exact `power_on`, ON status and normal-operation checks.
Separated controller-side transition from a later new host session after network readiness.
Rejected host-SSH origin, fixed sleep, insecure credentials, automatic retry/cycle and DUT action.

test_case.purpose: Verify one approved GPIO action from the always-on controller transitions the host from authoritative standby through correct rails/POST to OS Ready and healthy operation.
required_package: Powerctrl controller domain/version/hash/owner and secure transport
Exact power_on GPIO/rail pulse, response and idempotence semantics
Independent rail/chassis/UART observer and stage timeouts
One-transition approval, no-retry recovery and complete post-boot health oracle
test_case.test_command: After standby and maintenance approval, securely run `/usr/bin/powerctrl.sh power_on` once from the documented always-on controller; capture command and independent rail/UART/POST/OS timeline; only after OS network readiness open a separate verified host session for boot ID, uptime, devices, filesystems, services and logs.
test_case.expected_result: The command is accepted once, rails sequence correctly, POST completes and OS becomes ready within approved time; expected devices/filesystems/services are healthy and no new BMC/OS critical error occurs.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires verified initial standby, one controller-side action, complete standby→ON→OS Ready evidence and healthy system. Already-on/unknown start, wrong rail sequence, stalled POST, missing device/service, timeout or critical log fails/blocks per engineer; command exit alone is insufficient.
safety_gate: Confirm exact target and stable standby with no active workload.
Authorize one transition and maintain independent OOB/UART recovery.
Use secure controller identity; host SSH is post-boot evidence only.
No automatic retry, reset or power cycle on ambiguous failure.
expected_evidence: Separate secure host boot ID/uptime/device/filesystem/service/log health plus SEL and engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: On inconsistent standby, rail fault, POST stall or timeout, preserve evidence and stop. Use only the pre-approved recovery path; do not issue a second power_on or power cycle automatically.

source_conflict.reason: The source coherently describes standby-to-on; missing controller/GPIO/timing facts are project specifications, while host SSH is only a flawed prior-review substitution.

blocked.reason: The transition method is identifiable and becomes executable after owner-supplied semantics and recovery; it remains RPUC.
